extracted.intended_audience: colleges, universities, scholars, academic leaders, and humanities-focused organizations seeking Mellon Foundation funding
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance describing the Mellon Foundation's Higher Learning grantmaking: who is supported, the kinds of humanities work funded (research, curriculum, programming, partnerships), and the Foundation's typical invitation-based process and partnership priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — colleges and universities
rubrics_metrics.description: Colleges and universities exploring new directions in humanistic study in a range of learning environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon funds institutions of higher education that are experimenting with or expanding humanistic study across diverse learning settings (examples later in page: rural universities, tribal colleges, HBCUs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — scholars and academic leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholars and academic leaders working to deepen our understanding of American history and culture, advance new methods for scholarly interpretation, and elevate underrepresented perspectives in academia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support targets individuals and leaders whose work advances interpretive methods, enriches understanding of U.S. history and culture, and brings forward underrepresented viewpoints within the academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipients — humanities-focused organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanities-focused organizations committed to expanding public understanding and appreciation of the liberal arts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-academic organizations that have a clear commitment to public-facing humanities work and broadening appreciation for the liberal arts are within scope for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of funded activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic research, curricular development, extracurricular programming, internships, and community partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon funds a range of activities that support humanities education and scholarship — from research projects to programmatic and community-engaged efforts — reflecting a pluralistic approach to 'higher learning.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and institutional inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding includes institutions such as rural universities, tribal colleges, HBCUs, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes a diversity of institutional contexts and explicitly names historically underserved and geographically diverse institutions as part of its remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projects beyond traditional higher education
rubrics_metrics.description: We also fund humanities projects beyond colleges and universities that deepen our understanding of the United States, its cultures, and people, and help ensure the breadth of stories told and studied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mellon supports non-collegiate humanities initiatives that expand public knowledge about U.S. culture and history and that broaden whose stories are included in scholarship and public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership preference — expanding definitions of education
rubrics_metrics.description: We partner with institutions that are expanding the definition of education and learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is given to collaborators who are rethinking or broadening what education and learning can be — this can shape selection for institutional partnerships and program support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and invitation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Our staff seek out and get to know innovative organizations, scholars, and creators before inviting them to submit a proposal for funding. Most Mellon grants are made through these invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation typically funds via an invitation model: building relationships and identifying innovative potential partners prior to requesting proposals. Prospective applicants should note that many grants are not awarded through open unsolicited competitions.
